subject: SentryFlow x Redwood — integration scoping for LangChain/LlamaIndex + tracing
messages:
From: Diego Ramos <diego.r@sentryflow.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: SentryFlow x Redwood — initial scope for LangChain/LlamaIndex + tracing

Hi Karthik / Vanessa —

Thanks for taking this call last week. Per our conversation, SentryFlow (we're the observability layer for multi-model apps) would like to build a tight product integration with Redwood so customers using LangChain or LlamaIndex SDKs can get end-to-end traceability: prompt-level traces, model variant attribution, and cost token mapping.

Attached is a short MVP scope we sketched (sentryflow_mvp_scope_v1.pdf) and a rough architecture diagram. High-level asks from our side:
- A Redwood SDK adapter or example showing how to emit trace span metadata for LangChain/LlamaIndex runtimes.
- A stable correlation key in responses so we can stitch traces back to token-level events; prefer something that survives retries and fallback routing.
- Guidance on using Redwood Console metrics (per-route token counts) in our dashboards.

We'd like to propose a 30–45 minute technical sync next week to run the devs through a prototype flow and agree on an acceptance checklist. Are you available Wed or Thu morning PST?

Attaching: sentryflow_mvp_scope_v1.pdf (high-level), redwood_adapter_requirements.xlsx (a starter checklist).

Cheers,
Diego Ramos
Head of Integrations | SentryFlow
https://sentryflow.ai

--
SentryFlow Partnership Team <partnerships@sentryflow.ai>

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Ramos <diego.r@sentryflow.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SentryFlow x Redwood — initial scope for LangChain/LlamaIndex + tracing

Diego —

Appreciate the doc and the clear asks. Quick notes after a skim:
- We can ship a LangChain/LlamaIndex adapter pattern in two tiers: (A) example middleware for hosted Redwood API customers (sample code + tests) and (B) a Drop-In tracer shim for Redwood Private/Dedicated that preserves correlation headers and KV cache metadata.
- Correlation key: we prefer returning an "x-rw-trace" header populated with a stable request_id + model_variant; we'll confirm format. That will survive retry/fallback if the request is executed by the runtime (we'll call out edge cases where token-level attribution is partial).
- Console hooks: we can expose a per-route token attribution export (CSV + streaming webhook) for your ingestion pipeline.

Ask for our sync: Wed 2027-05-26 09:00–09:45 PT or Thu 2027-05-27 10:00–10:45 PT — which works? I'll bring an engineer who owns the LangChain adapter and Marissa for partner ops.

On Wed I'll also drop a short acceptance checklist (adapter tests, sample prompts, a perf budget for 1k reqs/min).

From: Diego Ramos <diego.r@sentryflow.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sylvia Park <sylvia.park@sentryflow.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SentryFlow x Redwood — initial scope for LangChain/LlamaIndex + tracing

Thanks Karthik — Wed 09:00 PT works for us. We'll come with a short demo of how SentryFlow currently ingests span metadata from LangChain agents (Node + Python examples). Two quick clarifications before the call:

1) Is the correlation header something Redwood will add automatically for hosted API customers, or do you want SDKs to forward a client-supplied request_id? We're trying to map implementation options to support both hosted and self-hosted customers.

2) For token-level attribution, what's the recommended lightweight export format you expect (CSV with start_token,end_token,model_variant,route_id)? If you already have a schema, please paste it in the drive doc so we can align.

Also — we'll bring our security lead (Sylvia) for a short section on data retention concerns; she may have a couple of pre-call questions about audit logs and retention windows.

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Ramos <diego.r@sentryflow.ai>, Sylvia Park <sylvia.park@sentryflow.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 May 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SentryFlow x Redwood — initial scope for LangChain/LlamaIndex + tracing

Diego / Sylvia —

Great to meet earlier — nice demos. Follow-ups from our side and next steps so we have a clean partner onboarding path: 

1) Security & data retention — Sylvia, thanks for the questions. Vanessa L. from Security will join the deeper discussion; preliminary: hosted customers can opt into per-route retention (24h, 7d, 30d) and Dedicated/Private customers can set retention via KMS policies. We'll share a short note on limits.

2) Correlation header approach — we prefer Redwood populate "x-rw-trace" for hosted API flows; for Private/Dedicated customers we'll provide the adapter so you can either pass through client request_id or derive one server-side. We'll add format details to the Drive doc.

3) Acceptance checklist — as promised, attaching draft_sow_sentryflow_redwood.docx and a short acceptance checklist in the Drive folder (link above). Key acceptance items: adapter unit tests (LangChain/LL Index), integration demo with 3 prompt templates, token attribution export validated on a 1k request sample.

4) Commercial / procurement — Marissa, can you own a quick commercial summary for SentryFlow? Diego, please share a standard MSA or procurement email contact so we can loop legal.

Next actions:
- Marissa to send commercial one-pager (by Tue next week)
- Karthik to open a dev-ticket for the LangChain adapter (we'll link to Github RFC)
- SentryFlow to populate token-export schema in Drive (Diego)

Thanks — looking forward to this.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Partnerships | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0142
